# `GammaAsymptotics.v2`

**Generated file - do not edit.**  Regenerated by `python scripts/ieantn.py pages`.

> The digamma asymptotic psi(w) = log w + O(1/\|w\|), restricted to a horizontal strip: for each height H a constant depending on H bounds \|\|psi w - log w\|\| by C/\|\|w\|\| whenever Re w >= 1 and \|Im w\| <= H. GammaAsymptotics.v1 states the same estimate on the whole half-plane and is retained, unproved, as the harder target; removing the height restriction means proving v1. The split exists because the strip is where the elementary argument reaches. v1's route -- iterating the digamma recurrence out of a compact box -- controls Re w -> infinity at bounded height and says nothing as Im w -> infinity, so v1 was over-general in precisely the direction carrying the difficulty. PROVED, and by way of Gauss' representation psi(s) = -gamma + sum_k (1/(k+1) - 1/(k+s)), which the solution establishes for every s with Re s > 0 and which Mathlib lists as a TODO in the file defining digamma. Mathlib carries no growth bound for digamma on this repository's pin. Every consumer so far wants only the strip. CH2.v1 evaluates psi at 1-s for s on a ladder whose every piece has \|Im s\| <= T.

## Conclusions

### `digamma_sub_log_isBigO_strip`

**Digamma is `log` up to `O(1/|w|)` on a horizontal strip.**

For each height `H` there is a constant, depending on `H`, with
`‖ψ w - log w‖ ≤ C / ‖w‖` whenever `1 ≤ Re w` and `|Im w| ≤ H`.

The constant is allowed to depend on `H` and that dependence is the whole point: a bound uniform
in `H` is `GammaAsymptotics.v1`, which is why that version is stated separately and left open.

Imports nothing: `w` is universally quantified with every condition a hypothesis, so a Lean proof
is this conclusion's whole justification.

```lean
def digamma_sub_log_isBigO_strip : Prop :=
  ∀ H : ℝ, ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ w : ℂ, 1 ≤ w.re → |w.im| ≤ H →
    ‖Complex.digamma w - Complex.log w‖ ≤ C / ‖w‖
```

**Justification `unjustified`** — none-yet

> Imports `none`, and that is a real none: w is universally quantified with every condition a hypothesis, so a Lean proof is the whole justification. SUPERSEDED, AND KEPT ONLY FOR THE ROUTE IT DESCRIBES. Solutions/GammaAsymptotics.v2 has since been through Comparator; the designated justification is the receipt below, not this. What follows is the account written before the proof existed, and ONE OF ITS CLAIMS TURNED OUT TO BE WRONG -- see the correction at the end. It is left standing because how it was wrong is more useful than a tidied version. THIS IS v1 WITH A HEIGHT RESTRICTION, and the restriction is the point. v1's recorded route -- iterate digamma_apply_add_one from a compact box in Re w in [1,2] -- DOES NOT PROVE v1. It pushes rightward and controls Re w -> infinity at bounded height; it says nothing about w = 1 + it as t -> infinity, which no compact box reaches. That was noticed only when someone went to carry the route out. THE STRIP DOES NOT RESCUE THE ELEMENTARY ROUTE EITHER, and an earlier version of this note claimed it did. Writing w = u + n with Re u in [1,2], the recurrence gives psi(w) = psi(u) + sum_{j<n} 1/(u+j), and comparing that sum with the harmonic series leaves psi(w) - log w -> psi(u) + gamma + sum_{j>=0} (1/(u+j) - 1/(1+j)) =: kappa(u), a 1-periodic analytic function. Pinning kappa == 0 IS the Gauss representation. psi(1) = -gamma gives kappa(1) = 0 and periodicity spreads it to the integers and no further; the trigamma route meets the same obstruction one derivative down. SO THE REAL TARGET IS THE GAUSS/WEIERSTRASS SERIES, psi(u) = -gamma + sum_{k>=0} (1/(k+1) - 1/(k+u)), which Mathlib does not have and lists as a TODO in the file defining digamma. Once it exists v2 follows directly; v1 needs a further uniformity argument as Im w -> infinity. That series is the thing worth formalizing, and it is a Mathlib contribution in its own right rather than a step private to this repository. THE CONSTANT MAY DEPEND ON H AND MUST. A bound uniform in H is exactly v1. WHERE THE ABOVE IS WRONG, and it is the paragraph beginning "THE STRIP DOES NOT RESCUE". Its argument runs through kappa(u) := lim (psi(u+n) - log(u+n)) and asserts that pinning kappa == 0 IS the Gauss representation. ON THE REALS THAT IS FALSE. Real.convexOn_log_Gamma gives \|psi(x) - log x\| <= 1/x directly, with the constant explicit and equal to 1, and kappa == 0 follows by letting n -> infinity -- no series, no integral representation, about a hundred lines. The obstruction the paragraph describes is real but sits one step later than it says: not in pinning kappa, but in getting from the real line to the complex plane, which is where the representation is genuinely needed and where the solution uses it. The rest of the note stands. Everything it says about v1 being over-general in the direction that carries the difficulty is exactly right, and v1 remains open.

## Limitations

Recorded by the node itself, not derived.

- WHAT THE RECEIPT COVERS IS THE IMPLICATION, AND THE HYPOTHESES ARE PART OF IT. Comparator accepted Solutions/GammaAsymptotics.v2 against this node's challenge under propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. That establishes the bound exactly where 1 <= Re w and \|Im w\| <= H hold, and nowhere else. THIS ENTRY PREVIOUSLY READ "Stated but not proved. Nothing downstream may treat it as established, and CH2.v1's ladder bounds inherit that." That was true until the solution landed and is kept here because the correction is the point: a limitation is a claim like any other and goes stale like any other.
- THE CONSTANT IS NOT UNIFORM IN THE HEIGHT, and that is the whole difference from v1. The solution produces C = (1 + 3H)(1 + H), which blows up as H grows; a bound uniform in H is exactly GammaAsymptotics.v1, which remains open. Nothing here bears on it -- the argument evaluates psi at the real point Re w and steps sideways by \|Im w\|, and that step costs a factor of the height.
- ONE ASYMPTOTIC ONLY, and a weak one. The node is named for the class because it is intended to grow: the -1/(2w) term, the sector version, a bound on Gamma itself, and Stirling's formula in the complex plane are all wanted and none is here. A consumer needing any of them will not find it.
- THE CONSTANT IS EXISTENTIAL. A consumer needing an explicit numerical constant -- which an explicit estimate eventually will -- cannot get one from this statement and will need a sharper conclusion stated alongside it.
- Re w >= 1 excludes the left half-plane entirely, where digamma has its poles. An application that needs psi there must combine this with the reflection formula psi(1-w) - psi(w) = pi cot(pi w). THAT IS NOW AVAILABLE: this entry previously said it awaited a more recent Mathlib than this repository's pin, and the bump that brought it (leanprover-community/mathlib4#42349) has since happened, so it is Complex.digamma_one_sub on the current pin. But note the reflection formula alone proves nothing about growth, in either half-plane, so having it does not shorten the work below. CH2.v1 does not need the left half-plane: its ladder argument evaluates psi at 1-s with Re(1-s) >= 2, which is already inside the stated range.
- No novelty is claimed. The expansion is classical.

## How this node was made

- **agent** (Claude Opus 5 (Anthropic)) — Established that Mathlib carries no digamma growth bound, identified the statement CH2's ladder argument needs, and chose the form, under the direction of the maintainer. THIS ENTRY PREVIOUSLY ENDED "No proof is claimed"; the solution has since been written and accepted by Comparator, so it does. The proof is original to this work in the sense that no source was followed for it, though the mathematics is classical. Its shape was found here rather than transcribed, and two turns are worth recording because the obvious route is different in each case. The real-variable estimate \|psi(x) - log x\| <= 1/x comes from Real.convexOn_log_Gamma alone -- log Gamma convex, so its derivative is monotone, and the mean value theorem traps log x between psi(x) and psi(x+1) -- with no series and no integral representation. And nowhere in the solution is psi differentiated: the two places that would naturally integrate psi' instead difference the Gauss series, where the divergent 1/(k+1) cancels and the remainder telescopes. Direction, review, and the choice of statement were the maintainer's throughout.
